sources.entry: Signal Desktop - Fast, simple, secure. Privacy that fits in your pocket. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/signalapp/Signal-Desktop)

summary.name: Signal Desktop
summary.one_liner: Signal Desktop is the desktop client for the Signal private messaging app, which must first be installed on a phone, and this page gives install instructions for Debian-based Linux.
use_cases: Install Signal desktop on Debian or Ubuntu
Set up the Signal AppImage on Linux
Verify a downloaded Signal AppImage with GPG
Send private messages from a computer
Keep Signal updated through the apt repository
summary.what_it_does: The page is the Signal download page and lists platforms Android, iOS, Linux, macOS, and Windows in its metadata. The visible text covers only Linux installation. For Debian-based 64-bit distributions, it gives steps to add the official signing key and apt repository, then install signal-desktop. It also gives an AppImage route: download the file, import the signing key, verify the GPG signature, and run it. The AppImage auto-updates, which can be configured in settings. The page states that Signal must first be installed on a phone to use the desktop app.
notable: Official apt repository install for Debian-based 64-bit Linux
AppImage with GPG signature verification and auto-update
Desktop client requires the Signal phone app to be installed first
Listed as open source (Signal-Desktop on GitHub) in awesome-mac
caveats: Linux apt instructions only work for 64-bit Debian-based distributions such as Ubuntu and Mint
Desktop app requires Signal to be installed on a phone first
